question.worked_solution:
First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So, we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x({tan}^{3}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x({tan}^{2}⁡x+1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-(-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}-(-2) \\  & =2-\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$
